newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds edge higher after U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds edge higher after U.S. data.

text.p: Irish bonds edged higher in thin afternoon trade on Thursday in line with European markets as U.S. Treasuries strengthened in mid-morning trade, dealers said.

A 2.2 per cent drop in the December Philadelphia Fed business index was likely to benefit U.S. Treasuries in the five-year-area while the long-end of the curve was firmer, with the three-year sector still seen strong, dealers said.
A larger-than-expected drop in the U.S. trade deficit in October to $7.99 billion also helped German bunds, dealers said.

"Prices are edging higher here as European markets strengthen on the back of good numbers from the U.S.," one dealer said. By 1530 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had edged up three pence from Wednesday's close to 101.30 to yield 6.36 percent while the eight percent bond due 2006 had improved by 10 pence from the close to 108.45 to yield 6.66 percent.
Dealers said there was still a lot of concern in the market about the Irish pound which was at 0.9945 stg from 0.9954 stg at the previous close.

"The weakness of the Irish pound against sterling is a worry, especially at the short-end. The Irish Central Bank has taken a back seat and if the punt falls to around 0.9900 then that is inflationary by nature," the dealer added.
